slides.texte_overlay:
7 boring skills that'll make you
dangerously capable in your 20s
Learn to make a phone call. Book the table, dispute the charge, call the landlord. Most people text and hope. The guy who just picks up the phone gets it sorted in four minutes.
Learn to read what you sign. Lease, job offer, gym membership. Find the cancellation clause and the auto-renewal before you sign. Nobody reads them, which is exactly why they work.
Learn to write a short email. Three lines. What you need, by when, and thanks. Long emails get skimmed. Short ones get answered before lunch.
Learn a little about everything. Five minutes a day on history, art or science. It sounds nerdy until you're the one at dinner who actually has something interesting to say.
slides.texte_sophia: Learn a little about everything. Five minutes a day on history, art or science. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app makes it easy, and suddenly you're the one at dinner with something to say.

slides.texte_overlay: Learn basic first aid. Burns, cuts, someone choking at the table. One afternoon class. You'll probably never need it, and the one time you do, you'll be the only calm person in the room.
Learn to negotiate. Rent, salary, a used car. Ask "Is that the best you can do?" and then stay quiet. It feels awkward for three seconds. The silence does most of the work.
Learn to leave on time. Set the alarm for when you need to walk out the door, not when you need to arrive. Showing up early is the most underrated flex there is.
